summary: The app's side navigation: sections of links to the main areas of Bridge, with the current page marked by a signal mark and an ink label.
whenToUse: Primary navigation of an app with more than five areas, in a left rail that stays visible.
Group items into titled sections by task (Library, Governance, Workspace).
collapsible on sections users rarely need, so the rail stays short.
count for items that need attention, like reviews waiting for you.
whenNotToUse: Switching views inside one page: use Tabs.
Fewer than five destinations: a top bar is enough.
Actions (Create token, Sync from Figma): put them in the page header as Buttons, not in the navigation.

dos.title: Mark exactly one current page
dos.text: active on the item for the current URL, including when the user is on a child page of it.

donts.title: Icons on some items only
donts.text: A ragged column of icons breaks the scan line. Use icons on every item of a section or none.

accessibility: A nav landmark: give it an aria-label when the page has other navigation (Breadcrumb, Pagination).
Each section is a list labelled by its title.
The current item has aria-current="page". It also gets a 2px signal mark and ink text, so color is not the only cue.
Collapsible section titles are buttons with aria-expanded (Base UI Collapsible); Enter and Space toggle them.
Items are full-width targets at the menu item height (36px comfortable, 30px compact).
contentGuidelines: Name destinations with nouns users know: "Tokens", "Reviews", "Settings".
Section titles are short nouns in sentence case, not all caps.
Counts are numbers only; explain them on the destination page.
